children: Liquidia said it entered a settlement agreement with United Therapeutics that fully resolves all pending litigation between the companies.

Under the terms of the deal, Liquidia will pay $380.7 million in multiple installments this year and next, which includes payments to resolve antitrust litigation against United Therapeutics. Liquidia will maintain uninterrupted access to Yutrepia, or treprostinil, for patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension, it added.
Shares for Liquidia rocketed 43%, to $38.31, in after-hours trading.

The settlement follows a Sept. 30 court ruling that certain patent claims are valid and infringed by Liquidia. The settlement includes mutual releases and is not an admission of liability by either party, and resolves all six ongoing lawsuits, Liquidia added.

The claims generally cover treatment of pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease with inhaled treprostinil, including dry powder formulations, Liquidia said. The company submitted a supplement to remove the PH-ILD indication from the Yutrepia label, and will no longer promote it for PH-ILD, it added.

The company submitted a supplement to remove the PH-ILD from the Yutrepia label, and will no longer promote it for PH-ILD, it added.

Liquidia said it will make a net payment to United Therapeutics of $175 million within 30 business days. The company will also pay $145.4 million in two equal installments due on or before Jan. 31, 2027, and April 30, 2027, respectively.
Liquidia said in connection with the settlement, it entered agreements with parties who have interests in antitrust litigation related to Treprostinil Injection.

Under the agreements, Liquidia will pay $60.3 million this month in full satisfaction of those parties' interests in the antitrust litigation, it said. The company said it concurrently terminated a promotional agreement tied to Treprostinil Injection and will no longer commercially support the product in the market.
